labelChirho: confusion, tumult, panic (divine or military disorder)
descriptionChirho: Noun meaning confusion, tumult, panic, or disorder, typically sent by God upon enemies or describing chaotic situations of war and judgment. Arabic اضْطِرَابٌ/اضْطِرَابُ 'disturbance/turmoil' is used consistently across all seven sense clusters with only minor inflectional variation (definite الاِضْطِرَابَ, plural اضْطِرَابَاتٌ, construct اضْطِرَابُ). Spanish 'confusión' (confusion) appears in nearly every instance, with 'tumultos' and 'turbación' as contextual synonyms. Korean 혼란 'confusion/chaos' (with particles 이/을/의/들) is uniform. Hindi covers the semantic range with हलचल 'commotion,' हड़बड़ाहट 'panic,' गड़बड़ 'disorder,' and उलझन 'confusion.' Swahili uses hofu 'fear,' machafuko 'chaos,' mkanganyiko 'confusion,' and fadhaa 'alarm.' All seven clusters represent grammatical variants (singular, plural, construct, with article, with conjunction) of the same core lexical meaning; there is no evidence of genuinely distinct sub-senses in the multilingual data.
